topic: Diagnostic reference levels for radiation dose

audits.title: Scan length as a major driver of CT radiation dose: a diagnostic reference level audit from Kosovo
audits.standard: German BfS 2022 diagnostic reference levels and Turkish reference values; local DRLs as 75th percentile
audits.setting: University Clinical Centre of Kosovo, 128-slice CT scanner

cycle1.result: 1,535 acquisitions analysed. Head CT (n = 590) CTDIvol 4.7% below BfS DRL but scan length 98.5% above orientation value (median 25.8 vs 13 cm); abdomen-pelvis scan length exceeded reference by 28%; coronary CTA CTDIvol +377%.

audits.intervention: Recommended: technologist landmarking training, protocol review and enabling iterative reconstruction.
audits.other_findings: Excess scan length, not CTDIvol, was the main driver of elevated dose.
audits.citation: Rudi G, Vula F, Bicaku A, Hoti KD, Ahmetgjekaj I. Scan length as a major driver of CT radiation dose: a diagnostic reference level audit from Kosovo. . 2026. doi:10.64898/2026.05.12.26353024.

audits.title: Establishment of National DRL for CT in Hybrid Imaging Studies (The Second Phase of the National NM CT (PET) Dose Audit for Kuwait Population -2019)
audits.standard: National diagnostic reference levels compared with UK, Swiss and French NDRLs
audits.setting: Eight PET centres, national multicentre audit

cycle1.result: First-phase national DRLs; figures not reported in this abstract.

audits.intervention: Not reported; second phase aimed to support optimisation and dose reduction.

cycle2.result: Head-body third quartile DLP 537 mGy·cm and CTDIvol 5 mGy (higher than UK NDRL 400, 4.3); whole-body proposed NDRLs 684, 4.1. Mean ED 6.9 mSv (HB) and 4.6 mSv (WB), lower than the first phase; 9.1% improvement in NDRL.

audits.citation: Masoomi M, Al-Shammeri I, Al-Kandari L, Elrahman H, Al-Shammari J. Establishment of National DRL for CT in Hybrid Imaging Studies (The Second Phase of the National NM CT (PET) Dose Audit for Kuwait Population -2019). . 2020. doi:10.1101/2020.09.20.20198176.

audits.title: Effect of clinical audits of radiation use in one hospital district in Finland.
audits.standard: Generally accepted standards for good medical radiological procedures (audit criteria list)
audits.setting: All imaging units in the southwest hospital district of Finland; external clinical audits by independent experts

cycle1.result: All units used radiation in accordance with requirements; 80 recommendations made, most (22/80) on instructions for the fundamental practice of examining a patient.

audits.intervention: Recommendations from the first audit implemented by units.

cycle2.result: Audit criteria fulfilled clearly better; 53 recommendations made, most in the category of radiation doses.

audits.other_findings: Most recommendations from the first audit had been taken into consideration by the second audit.
audits.citation: Hirvonen-Kari M, Salo S, Dean K, Kivisaari L. Effect of clinical audits of radiation use in one hospital district in Finland. Acta Radiol. 2009;50(4):389-395. doi:10.1080/02841850902755260. PMID: 19241189.

audits.title: An audit of diagnostic reference levels in interventional cardiology and radiology: are there differences between academic and non-academic centres?
audits.standard: Diagnostic reference levels (dose-area product, fluoroscopy time, number of images)

cycle1.result: No difference for cardiology procedures; lower doses for lower-limb procedures in non-academic centres, with wide variation.

audits.citation: Samara ET, Aroua A, De Palma R, Stauffer JC, Schmidt S, Trueb PR, et al.. Radiat Prot Dosimetry. 2012;148(1):74-82. doi:10.1093/rpd/ncq600. PMID: 21335331.

audits.title: Dose audit for patients undergoing two common radiography examinations with digital radiology systems.
audits.standard: EU and IAEA diagnostic reference levels for PA chest and AP KUB radiography
audits.setting: Five X-ray rooms at four hospitals, Ankara region

cycle1.result: Average entrance surface doses for chest exceeded international DRLs in two X-ray rooms of one computed radiography hospital; all other measurements approximately equal to or below DRLs.

audits.other_findings: Problems included improper exposure settings and uncalibrated automatic exposure control.
audits.citation: İnal T, Ataç G. Dose audit for patients undergoing two common radiography examinations with digital radiology systems. Diagn Interv Radiol. 2014;20(1):100-104. doi:10.5152/dir.2013.12122. PMID: 24317331.

audits.title: Patient dosimetry audit for establishing local diagnostic reference levels for nuclear medicine CT.
audits.standard: Proposed National Diagnostic Reference Levels for nuclear medicine CT
audits.setting: Nuclear medicine CT, University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: For most examinations mean dose-length products did not exceed proposed national reference levels; bone SPECT/CT lumbar spine DLPs ranged from 51 ± 5 mGy cm (low dose) to 1086 ± 124 mGy cm (metal dose).

audits.other_findings: The audit process was labour intensive because of limited CRIS data, reliance on paper records and small numbers after subdivision.
audits.citation: Gardner M, Katsidzira NM, Ross E, Larkin EA. Patient dosimetry audit for establishing local diagnostic reference levels for nuclear medicine CT. Br J Radiol. 2017;90(1071):20160850. doi:10.1259/bjr.20160850. PMID: 28102707.

audits.title: Patient-Based Dose Audit for Common Radiographic Examinations With Digital Radiology Systems: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
audits.standard: International diagnostic reference levels (IDRLs) and UK DRLs for dose area product
audits.setting: Medical imaging department, Ministry of the National Guard - Health Affairs, Jeddah (retrospective)

cycle1.result: 75th percentile DAP below IDRLs for all examinations except lateral lumbar, AP and lateral thoracic spine, which exceeded IDRLs by up to 40.7%, 2.8% and 365.5%.

audits.other_findings: Mean DAP significantly exceeded UK DRLs for lateral thoracic and lateral lumbar spine; 699 examinations in total.
audits.citation: Alshamrani KM, Alkenawi AA, Alghamdi BN, Honain RH, Alshehri HA, Alshatiri MO, et al.. Patient-Based Dose Audit for Common Radiographic Examinations With Digital Radiology Systems: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study. Cureus. 2021;13(5):e15005. doi:10.7759/cureus.15005. PMID: 34150373.

audits.title: An audit of patient radiation doses in interventional radiology at a South African hospital.
audits.standard: Published local and international diagnostic reference levels (ICRP optimisation)

cycle1.result: Local DRLs for diagnostic cerebral angiogram (209.3) and interventional cerebral angiogram (275) exceeded published ranges; uterine artery embolisation exceeded ranges for KAP (954.9 Gy/cm2) and Ka,r (2640.8 mGy).

audits.other_findings: Percutaneous transhepatic biliary drainage was the commonest procedure (n=146, 25.9%).
audits.citation: Slave O, Mahomed N. An audit of patient radiation doses in interventional radiology at a South African hospital. SA J Radiol. 2023;27(1):2559. doi:10.4102/sajr.v27i1.2559. PMID: 36756356.

audits.title: OPTIMIZATION OF RADIATION DOSE IN CT IMAGING: ESTABLISHING THE INSTITUTIONAL DIAGNOSTIC REFERENCE LEVELS AND PATIENT DOSE AUDITING.
audits.standard: National and international diagnostic reference levels; proposed local DRLs
audits.setting: Advanced Medical and Dental Institute, Universiti Sains Malaysia, Penang

cycle1.result: Most proposed local DRLs exceeded national DRLs (63%) and international DRLs (67%); almost half of 2018 dose data exceeded the proposed local DRLs.

audits.other_findings: Unusually high doses in TAP, brain/head and pelvis CT, possibly from higher mAs, more contrast phases and pitch.
audits.citation: Razali MASM, Ahmad MZ, Shuaib IL, Osman ND. OPTIMIZATION OF RADIATION DOSE IN CT IMAGING: ESTABLISHING THE INSTITUTIONAL DIAGNOSTIC REFERENCE LEVELS AND PATIENT DOSE AUDITING. Radiat Prot Dosimetry. 2020;188(2):213-221. doi:10.1093/rpd/ncz278. PMID: 31885043.
